articles.title: Kamala Harris calls to expand Supreme Court, add states if Dems take Congress
articles.summary: Kamala Harris called for Supreme Court expansion and Electoral College changes, and a legal expert warned her proposals could set a dangerous precedent.
articles.body:
Former Vice President Kamala Harris called for institutional changes to the Supreme Court and the Electoral College during an interview Tuesday, calling for more justices on the highest court in the nation.

"The work that we can do about winning back the House and the Senate is going to be on a number of things. For example, I believe that we need to expand the Supreme Court . We need more justices on the Supreme Court so that we can have a court that actually reinforces the spirit and principles behind the Constitution of the United States," Harris told podcast host Keke Palmer on her "Baby, This is Keke Palmer" podcast.

"I believe that we should be pushing for what is possible around changing the Electoral College. Right?

"It's about, the popular vote has to matter, right? You know, all the things that make people feel, like, overwhelmed, and does their vote matter? We have, you know, listen, if the folks there want it, we should be pushing for statehood for Puerto Rico and D.C., right? These are some of the things that are structural that we need to do, but we need to reestablish affordable child care," Harris added .

Harris lost both the Electoral College and the popular vote to President Donald Trump in 2024. She told Palmer she still remains undecided about a 2028 presidential run.

Y. David Scharf, chairman of Morrison Cohen LLP and head of its government strategies & controversies practice, told Fox News Digital that Harris' proposed changes could set a "dangerous precedent."

"Kamala Harris says she wants to defend democracy, but her solution is to rewrite its rules when Democrats don't like the results. That's a dangerous precedent," he said. "Nine justices have been the number since 1869. FDR tried to pack the Supreme Court, and even his own party pushed back. Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg herself warned that expanding the court would make it look partisan.

"The Electoral College is written into the Constitution. Eliminating it requires a constitutional amendment, not a Democratic majority in Congress. You don't get to change the referee because you don't like the calls. Harris may think this is a winning message for the Democratic base, but it's a much tougher sell to the independent and swing voters her party needs."

The former VP also spoke about the midterm elections during the interview.

"On the first Tuesday in November, the midterms are going to happen," Harris said. "And our ability to put people in Congress who will say no, when they do things like cut $1 trillion out of Medicaid will be powerful and affect people right away.

"Our ability to put people in Congress who will say enough of the corruption, enough of ending the funding for research on issues like fibroids, which they have done under the guise of attacking DEI, can be stopped. There are things that are not only about what will be helpful, but also stopping what is harmful, that we can do right away with these midterm elections."

Her comments come days after her 2024 vice presidential running mate, Gov. Tim Walz, warned of a reckoning among Democrats if the party fails to deliver on promises should they take back Congress and potentially the presidency in 2028.

Harris was called out by Democratic advisors Tuesday for failing to reinvent herself politically as she weighs another White House run, Politico reported .

The report, based on interviews with nearly 20 California-based Democratic donors and strategists, highlighted growing skepticism among some party insiders about Harris' political future and whether she has done enough to distinguish herself from her unsuccessful 2024 campaign.

Longtime Democratic strategist Doug Herman, a veteran of former President Barack Obama's 2008 and 2012 campaigns, told Politico that Harris "totally blew it. … She hasn't gotten into the mix."

Former Gov. Jim Hodges of South Carolina , the leadoff state in the Democratic Party's 2028 presidential nominating calendar, told the outlet, "I don't see anything different myself. It seems like more of the same to me."

Veteran Democratic strategist Maria Cardona, an outside advisor to Harris, pushed back against the criticism highlighted in a new Politico report and called the story "infuriating" in a previous statement to Fox News Digital.

"How can you state that she hasn't done anything new or groundbreaking or talked about new initiatives or policies and then lay out exactly those policies — like proposing an expanded Supreme Court, lowering the voting age to 16, making D.C. and Puerto Rico states. Those are pretty groundbreaking policies," Cardona told Fox News Digital, as she pointed to some of Harris' moves since the end of former President Joe Biden's administration.

articles.title: The 3rd Circuit Upholds the Gun Rights of a Man Who Committed a Nonviolent Misdemeanor 2 Decades Ago
articles.summary: The appeals court said it was unconstitutional to permanently disarm Edward Williams based on a 2005 DUI conviction.
articles.body:
Thanks to a 2005 DUI conviction in Pennsylvania, Edward Williams permanently lost the constitutional right to keep and bear arms. But he did not realize that until a decade later, and his confusion on that point is understandable.

The federal law that stripped Williams of his Second Amendment rights is commonly described as applying to "felons," and Williams' offense was a misdemeanor. But although his sentence did not include any time behind bars, his crime theoretically could have sent him to prison for up to five years. That was enough to trigger 18 USC 922(g)(1) , which covers anyone convicted of "a crime punishable by imprisonment for a term exceeding one year."

When a lawyer alerted Williams to that wrinkle, which made his continued ownership of firearms a federal felony, he got rid of his guns. But he did not think that requirement was fair, reasonable, or constitutional, and this week a federal appeals court agreed. The U.S. Court of Appeals for the 3rd Circuit recognized a historical tradition of disarming "physically dangerous individuals" whose possession of firearms would pose a threat to public safety. But it said Williams plainly does not fit into that category.

"The federal government spent nearly a decade trying to permanently disarm a peaceable man over a nonviolent misdemeanor—and it lost bigly," says Brandon Combs, president of the Firearms Policy Coalition, which supported Williams' lawsuit. "The government does not get to turn a nonviolent conviction into a lifetime ban on exercising a constitutionally protected right."

The 3rd Circuit's en banc decision in Williams v. Attorney General affirms a 2023 ruling by a federal judge who likewise concluded that disarming Williams was unconstitutional. It elaborates on the logic of Range v. Attorney General , a 2023 decision that restored the gun rights of a Pennsylvania man who had been convicted of food stamp fraud. In both cases, the 3rd Circuit held that applying Section 922(g)(1) to the plaintiffs was not "consistent with this Nation's historical tradition of firearm regulation"—the Second Amendment test established by the Supreme Court's 2022 decision in New York State Rifle & Pistol Association v. Bruen .

Writing for the majority in Williams' case, 3rd Circuit Judge Paul Matey acknowledges that the Supreme Court has described "longstanding prohibitions on the possession of firearms by felons" as "presumptively lawful." But "those longstanding customs restricted the violently dangerous (within which some felons would be included), not felons writ large," he says. "Felons were restricted because they posed a physical danger, rather than for their offense of conviction."

Matey argues that "focusing on physical dangerousness corrects the erroneous argument" that "only law-abiding and responsible citizens can exercise the rights protected by the Second Amendment"—a claim that the Supreme Court rejected in the 2024 case United States v. Rahimi . "We find no history that supports disarming irresponsible people, where 'responsible' is defined by the whim of the sovereign or the will of the majority," he says, alluding to the danger of allowing legislators to whittle away at the Second Amendment by criminalizing an ever-widening range of conduct.

Matey emphasizes "the novelty of forever restricting all felons from possessing firearms for lawful purposes." The original restriction, which Congress approved in 1938 as part of the Federal Firearms Act , applied only to violent crimes such as murder, manslaughter, rape, kidnapping, robbery, and assault with a deadly weapon. In 1961, Congress expanded the ban to cover nonviolent crimes punishable by more than a year in prison.

Williams' 2005 DUI conviction qualified for two reasons. He had a prior DUI conviction, stemming from a 2000 arrest in State College. And when he was arrested again in Philadelphia four years later, his blood alcohol concentration was a whopping 0.223 percent. That made his second offense a first-degree misdemeanor, which carries a maximum prison sentence of five years.

Since then, Williams has stayed out of trouble. "He has done nothing violent, let alone dangerous, for over twenty years, and has held steady employment at the same job for over three decades," Matey notes. Williams drinks only occasionally, and a psychological evaluation found he "has a normal personality, without psychopathology and without addiction or violent tendencies."

The Justice Department nevertheless argued that Williams' continuing disarmament is consistent with the Bruen test, which requires historical analogs that are "relevantly similar" in motivation and scope. In making that case, the government relied mainly on early laws aimed at "habitual drunkards"—the same analogy that the Supreme Court unanimously rejected last June in United States v. Hemani , which involved the federal ban on gun possession by "unlawful" drug users.

Although the Justice Department "acknowledges it may proscribe Williams's possession of firearms only if he 'presently poses a physical danger if armed,'" Matey says, it "offers no evidence to establish this as the aim of the habitual drunkard laws." Those laws, the Supreme Court noted in Hemani , "did not seek to protect the public from violence so much as to protect habitual drunkards from themselves and their families from financial devastation."

Nor did the habitual drunkard laws permanently disarm people, as Section 922(g)(1) does. "Most statutes capped the commitment of habitual drunkards to the state inebriate asylum, prison, or hard labor to a few months or years," Matey notes. "Others provided for an indefinite period of incarceration, but had no indication that upon release individuals continued to forfeit their arms. Rather, once someone was 'safe' to 'go at large,' they were restored to the status of a full rights-bearing citizen."

Contrary to the considerations that the Supreme Court deemed relevant in Hemani , Matey says, the Justice Department "fails to show that Williams threatens to 'misuse[] a gun while intoxicated,' or that he 'poses a danger to himself or others as a result' of alcohol abuse. In fact, much like those nineteenth-century drunkards released from custody and restored their rights, the record shows that Williams poses no present physical danger from the use of a firearm, or anything else."

The 3rd Circuit is one of three federal appeals courts that have allowed people with nonviolent felony records to argue that Section 922(g)(1) is unconstitutional as applied to them. But such challenges have been blocked in six circuits, notwithstanding compelling historical evidence that the law reaches much farther than the Second Amendment allows. So far, the Supreme Court has declined to accept any of the many petitions asking it to resolve that circuit split.

articles.title: Dark Horse: PF pede prorrogação de inquérito que envolve Flávio | G1
articles.standfirst: Cinebiografia tornou-se alvo de investigação no STF sobre o financiamento do filme por Vorcaro, do Master, e a atuação de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), candidato à Presidência, no caso.
articles.summary: A PF investiga no Caso Dark Horse o financiamento da cinebiografia de Bolsonaro por Daniel Vorcaro e a suposta atuação do senador Flávio Bolsonaro no esquema.
articles.body:
A Polícia Federal (PF) pediu ao ministro André Mendonça , do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), a prorrogação do inquérito que investiga o financiamento do filme Dark Horse, que trata da história do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro (PL), por 90 dias.

A cinebiografia tornou-se alvo de investigação no STF sobre o financiamento do filme pelo ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro, ex-dono do Banco Master, e a atuação do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), candidato à Presidência da República, no caso.

O inquérito, aberto em julho a pedido da Polícia Federal e com parecer favorável da Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR), investiga suspeitas de lavagem de dinheiro, evasão de divisas, corrupção e outros possíveis crimes relacionados ao financiamento da produção.

Flávio Bolsonaro aparece formalmente como investigado.

Em outra frente, relatada pelo ministro Flávio Dino, a PF investiga suspeitas de desvio de emendas parlamentares indicadas pelo deputado federal Mario Frias (PL) a entidades ligadas a Karina Ferreira da Gama, proprietária da Go Up Entertainment, produtora de "Dark Horse". ( Veja mais detalhes )

Uma empresa ligada a Vorcaro teria enviado recursos aos Estados Unidos. A PF passou a buscar o rastreamento dos valores e a apurar se o dinheiro foi efetivamente aplicado na produção cinematográfica.

A dona da Go Up, Karina Ferreira da Gama, afirmou em maio à GloboNews e à TV Globo que Vorcaro foi responsável por mais de 90% dos recursos que viabilizaram a produção.

💵 Segundo ela, o orçamento realizado até então estava em cerca de US$ 13 milhões, equivalentes a R$ 65,7 milhões à época. Flávio Bolsonaro havia admitido que Vorcaro colocou pouco mais de US$ 12 milhões no projeto.

Senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), candidato à Presidência da República — Foto: Carlos Moura/Agência Senado

os repasses feitos por Vorcaro a pedido de Flávio Bolsonaro;

a possibilidade de parte dos recursos ter sido usada para custear Eduardo Bolsonaro nos Estados Unidos; e

a destinação de emendas parlamentares a entidades relacionadas à produtora do longa.

Eduardo Bolsonaro negou ter recebido recursos de fundo ligado a Vorcaro. Disse que seu status migratório nos Estados Unidos não permitiria esse tipo de repasse e afirmou ter informado às autoridades americanas a origem de seus recursos.

Na mesma época, veio a público um contrato em que Eduardo Bolsonaro aparecia como produtor-executivo de "Dark Horse".

Outra investigação apura emendas ligadas à produtora

Outra investigação sob responsabilidade do ministro Flávio Dino analisa o envio de recursos públicos a organizações ligadas à proprietária da produtora de "Dark Horse".

Entre as entidades estão o Instituto Conhecer Brasil (ICB) e a Academia Nacional de Cultura (ANC), presididos por Karina Ferreira da Gama. A Go Up Entertainment não foi alvo dos mandados de busca.

Mario Frias, que atua como roteirista e produtor-executivo de "Dark Horse", afirmou ao STF em maio que as emendas destinadas às organizações não foram enviadas para financiar a produção cinematográfica.

Em 10 de setembro, PF e Controladoria-Geral da União (CGU) deflagraram a operação Make Up. Foram cumpridos 49 mandados de busca e apreensão no Distrito Federal, em São Paulo, no Rio de Janeiro e no Ceará, autorizados por Flávio Dino.

Mario Frias e Karina Ferreira da Gama estavam entre os alvos. São investigados possíveis crimes de peculato, falsidade documental, lavagem de dinheiro, organização criminosa e crimes licitatórios.

Um relatório da PF apontou ainda coincidência temporal entre movimentações financeiras da Go Up e o repasse das emendas destinadas por Mario Frias ao Instituto Conhecer Brasil.

Os investigadores levantaram a suspeita de que recursos públicos possam ter custeado despesas como hospedagem, refeições e pagamentos a outras produtoras durante o período de produção do filme.

Defesa tentou levar investigação de Dino para Mendonça

Os advogados sustentaram que, como Mendonça já estava à frente de outras apurações relacionadas ao filme, deveria ficar também com a investigação sobre emendas parlamentares.

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro visita sede da Globo no Rio | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do PL foi recebido pelo presidente do Grupo Globo, João Roberto Marinho, e pelo vice-presidente de Relações Institucionais, Paulo Tonet. O encontro não contou com a presença de lideranças do Jornalismo.

articles.body:
O candidato à Presidência Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) visitou a sede da Globo, no Rio de janeiro, nesta sexta-feira (16) e foi recebido pelo presidente do Grupo Globo, João Roberto Marinho, e pelo vice-presidente de Relações Institucionais, Paulo Tonet. articles.title: Redução do IPVA em Minas Gerais: Governo envia proposta de 75% | G1
articles.standfirst: Texto depende de aprovação dos deputados e de regulamentação. Próxima gestão poderá avaliar a redução e definir os percentuais. Redução do imposto foi promessa de campanha do governador eleito, Cleitinho Azevedo (Republicanos).
articles.summary: O governo de Minas Gerais enviou à ALMG um projeto que permite a redução do IPVA em até 75%, cumprindo promessa de campanha do governador eleito.
articles.body:
Governo de Minas envia à ALMG proposta que permite reduzir IPVA em até 75% — Foto: Gil Leonardi/Imprensa MG/Divulgação

O governo de Minas Gerais enviou à Assembleia Legislativa (ALMG) um projeto de lei que permite reduzir em até 75% as alíquotas do Imposto sobre a Propriedade de Veículos Automotores (IPVA). A diminuição do tributo era uma promessa de campanha do governador eleito, Cleitinho Azevedo (Republicanos).

A proposta não estabelece um desconto automático. Se o texto for aprovado, caberá à próxima gestão avaliar se haverá redução e definir os percentuais, mediante regulamentação.

Em nota, o Executivo afirmou que a iniciativa busca viabilizar a análise da medida pelo próximo governo, em consonância com a proposta defendida pelo governo eleito.

Segundo o governo estadual, a aprovação ainda em 2026 permitirá que essa avaliação considere a cobrança do próximo ano. Isso porque o fato gerador do IPVA — a situação que dá origem à cobrança do imposto — ocorre em 1º de janeiro de cada ano.

O projeto também autoriza o Executivo a preservar os valores que seriam destinados às prefeituras caso as alíquotas sejam reduzidas.

Pela proposta, o governo poderá assegurar aos municípios o repasse integral dos recursos que receberiam com a arrecadação do IPVA. A aplicação dessa medida também dependerá de regulamentação.

A nota não detalha quais categorias de veículos poderão ser beneficiadas, os percentuais que poderão ser adotados nem o impacto estimado sobre a arrecadação estadual.

O envio da proposta ocorre em meio a críticas de Cleitinho ao atual governador, Mateus Simões (PSD) . Durante discurso no Senado nesta quinta-feira (15), o governador eleito questionou o aumento da previsão de déficit nas contas de Minas para 2027, de R$ 8,87 bilhões para R$ 10,51 bilhões.

“Que preparo é esse pelo estado? Que até então, antes, na campanha, o estado estava mil maravilhas. Agora, a partir de 1º de janeiro, o estado quebrou?”, afirmou.

Cleitinho também disse que fará uma auditoria e revisará todos os contratos ao assumir o governo.

Em resposta às declarações, o governo de Minas reafirmou o compromisso com a transparência e afirmou que o déficit previsto no orçamento não necessariamente se concretizará. A gestão também disse que a transição ocorre de forma transparente e profissional e que caberá ao futuro governo fazer os ajustes que considerar adequados.

Após o discurso, Cleitinho passou mal e foi atendido pela equipe de saúde do Senado . Segundo nota médica encaminhada pela assessoria do senador, ele apresentou pico de pressão arterial e frequência cardíaca um pouco elevada.

Os exames de eletrocardiograma e enzimas cardíacas tiveram resultados normais. Após receber medicação e hidratação, ele apresentou melhora e foi liberado em bom estado, com orientação de repouso.

articles.title: Padre Júlio Lancellotti celebra missa de 7º dia de Telma de Souza   | G1
articles.standfirst: Cerimônia será realizada às 14h deste sábado (17), na Catedral de Santos. Ex-prefeita morreu aos 82 anos.
articles.summary: Cerimônia será realizada às 14h deste sábado (17), na Catedral de Santos. Ex-prefeita morreu aos 82 anos.
articles.body:
Padre Júlio Lancellotti celebra missa de sétimo dia da ex-prefeita Telma de Souza em Santos, SP — Foto: Divulgação/Instituto Telma de Souza

A missa de sétimo dia em homenagem à ex-prefeita Telma de Souza (PT) será celebrada pelo padre Júlio Lancellotti neste sábado (17), na Catedral de Santos , no litoral de São Paulo. A cerimônia está marcada para as 14h.

Telma morreu aos 82 anos, no Hospital Mont Serrat, na Vila Mathias. Única mulher eleita para comandar a Prefeitura de Santos, ela participou da fundação do Partido dos Trabalhadores (PT), foi deputada estadual e exerceu três mandatos como deputada federal por São Paulo.

A Catedral de Santos fica na Praça Patriarca José Bonifácio, no Centro. Além de Júlio Lancellotti, participarão da missa o pároco José Paulo, sacerdotes da Diocese e o Coral Municipal.

De acordo com o Instituto Telma de Souza, a amizade entre a ex-prefeita e o padre Júlio Lancellotti era de longa data.

O sacerdote participou do "Seminário Regional Políticas para a População em Situação de Rua - diagnóstico, experiência e garantia de direitos", realizado no ano passado pelo Instituto Telma de Souza, com aproximadamente 500 participantes.

Em 2019, durante um dos mandatos de Telma como vereadora na Câmara Municipal de Santos, o religioso também esteve na cidade para participar de uma audiência pública sobre o assunto.

Telma de Souza (PT) participou do debate na sede do Grupo Tribuna, em Santos (SP), em 2024 — Foto: Alexsander Ferraz/A Tribuna Jornal

Telma Sandra Augusto de Souza nasceu em Santos em 29 de setembro de 1944. Ela era filha de João Inácio de Souza, o Joãozinho do Instituto, vereador cassado em 1964 pela ditadura, e da também ex-vereadora Hilda Augusto de Souza.

Uma das fundadoras do PT, em 1980, Telma foi vereadora entre 1983 e 1986, deputada estadual em 1987 e 1988 e prefeita de Santos de 1989 a 1992.

Ela também exerceu três mandatos como deputada federal, entre 1995 e 2007, e voltou à Câmara de Santos como vereadora entre 2017 e 2024.

Telma de Souza enquanto prefeita de Santos, entre 1989 e 1992 — Foto: Arquivo A Tribuna Jornal

A ex-prefeita morreu às 20h27 de sábado (10). Ela estava internada no Hospital Mont Serrat, na Vila Mathias, após sofrer um acidente vascular cerebral (AVC) e ter uma infecção urinária.

Telma já havia se recuperado de um AVC isquêmico sofrido cerca de um ano antes e, desde então, restringido as participações em eventos públicos.

Diversas autoridades, munícipes, amigos e familiares participaram da cerimônia de velório e sepultamento de Telma , no último domingo (11). Na terça-feira (13), uma jabuticabeira em alusão ao legado da ex-prefeita foi plantada no pátio do Sindicato dos Petroleiros do Litoral Paulista (SindiPetro).

Nas redes sociais, lideranças políticas de diferentes regiões do país lamentaram a morte da ex-prefeita. Entre as homenagens, o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) destacou o legado da petista na criação de políticas públicas de saúde mental e de prevenção e tratamento da Aids.

articles.title: Corregedor do TSE nega pedido de Flávio Bolsonaro para proibir gravações eleitorais no Planalto e no Alvorada | G1
articles.standfirst: Ministro Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva afirmou que medidas preventivas devem apontar com precisão a conduta a ser impedida e ressaltou que a decisão não impede a apuração de eventuais ilícitos eleitorais.
articles.summary: Ministro Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva afirmou que medidas preventivas devem apontar com precisão a conduta a ser impedida e ressaltou que a decisão não impede a apuração de eventuais ilícitos eleitorais.
articles.body:
O corregedor-geral da Justiça Eleitoral, ministro Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva, negou nesta sexta-feira (16) um pedido do candidato à Presidência Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) para proibir, de forma genérica, a realização de lives, podcasts, entrevistas e gravações de conteúdo eleitoral nos palácios do Planalto e da Alvorada.

O pedido foi apresentado em uma ação de investigação judicial eleitoral (AIJE) contra a chapa do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o vice-presidente Geraldo Alckmin, em tramitação no Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).

Na ação, Flávio afirma que houve abuso de poder político e de autoridade por meio do uso de eventos, bens, serviços e estruturas da administração pública em benefício de candidatura presidencial.

Ao rejeitar a proibição, Cueva afirmou que medidas preventivas devem indicar de forma precisa a conduta que se pretende impedir.

Segundo o ministro, o pedido exigiria uma análise antecipada de conteúdos que ainda não foram produzidos e poderia impor restrições excessivas à comunicação política e ao exercício das atribuições institucionais.

Entre as medidas de urgência solicitadas, estão restrições ao uso de imagens do pronunciamento de Lula na Assembleia Geral das Nações Unidas, a remoção de conteúdos e a preservação de provas.

Na decisão, Cueva ressaltou ainda que a rejeição das medidas não autoriza o uso indevido da estrutura pública em benefício de candidaturas e não impede a investigação e eventual responsabilização por ilícitos eleitorais.

Emas no Palácio da Alvorada, em imagem de arquivo — Foto: Presidência da República/Reprodução

articles.title: TSE mantém decisão que determinou que Meta não interfira em distribuição de conteúdo político-eleitoral   | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão foi dada em ação protocolada pela campanha do presidente Lula à reeleição, após dizer que a empresa, responsável pelo Facebook, Instagram e WhatsApp, "tem falhado, de forma reiterada e sistemática, na entrega de postagens da coligação".
articles.summary: Decisão foi dada em ação protocolada pela campanha do presidente Lula à reeleição, após dizer que a empresa, responsável pelo Facebook, Instagram e WhatsApp, "tem falhado, de forma reiterada e sistemática, na entrega de postagens da coligação".
articles.body:
Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Lula (PT) disputam o 2º turno — Foto: Diego Herculano/Reuters e Adriano Machado/Reuters

O Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) manteve, por unanimidade, a decisão do ministro Marco Aurélio Bellizze que determinou, que até o fim do segundo turno das eleições, sob pena de multa diária de R$ 500 mil, a Meta não interfira na distribuição de conteúdo político-eleitoral nem de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), nem de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL).

A decisão foi dada em ação protocolada pela campanha do presidente Lula à reeleição , após dizer que a empresa, responsável pelo Facebook, Instagram e WhatsApp, "tem falhado, de forma reiterada e sistemática, na entrega de postagens da coligação".

A campanha também mencionou que comandos para geração de imagens de inteligência artificial não permitem a criação de conteúdos sobre Lula. Ainda de acordo com a petição, a criação de imagens relacionadas ao candidato Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) está liberada.

Segundo a coligação, há indícios de tratamento desigual na distribuição de conteúdos políticos pela plataforma.

Os advogados da coligação afirmam ainda que perfis ligados à candidatura adversária, entre eles o do deputado Nikolas Ferreira, registrariam números de visualizações considerados incompatíveis com os parâmetros usuais da plataforma.

A decisão do ministro Marco Aurélio Bellizze determina que a

não aplique a conteúdos políticos-eleitorais relativos a qualquer das candidaturas que disputam o segundo turno medidas de redução de distribuição, de exclusão de recomendação, ou de restrição de busca;

precisa, no prazo de 24 horas, limitar a exclusão dos sistemas de recomendação aos perfis oficiais; e

desabilite ou restrinja as contas de anúncios das candidaturas.

Ainda de acordo com a decisão, a empresa precisa assegurar que a Meta AI aplique critério idêntico às candidaturas.

🔎 A Meta AI é um assistente de inteligência artificial gratuito e integrado ao WhatsApp, Instagram e Facebook. Ela funciona de forma semelhante ao ChatGPT nos serviços da Meta e, a partir de descrições simples, pode produzir textos, planejar atividades e criar imagens, por exemplo.

"Considerando que a ferramenta está ao alcance de qualquer usuário do WhatsApp, a dez dias do segundo turno, justifica-se a determinação de que mantenha critério idêntico às duas candidaturas, abstendo-se de gerar peças de propaganda eleitoral favoráveis ou contrárias a qualquer delas, e de que a representada esclareça os critérios empregados", disse o ministro na decisão.

Na decisão, o ministro afirmou que não está comprovado que houve uma manipulação deliberada, mas que é preciso aprofundar a análise. Isso porque fatos relevantes ocorrem em ambiente que somente a Meta controla. Bellizze ressaltou ainda que, nesses casos, a atuação da Justiça Eleitoral deve observar a menor interferência possível no debate democrático.

O TSE determinou que a empresa apure 255 perfis e das 1.204 publicações.

O ministro pediu informações em 48h sobre a atuação nas eleições, como medidas aplicadas ao perfil do deputado federal Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) desde 16 de agosto de 2026 e a discriminação do alcance das publicações dos perfis oficiais dos dois candidatos à Presidência da República, entre 1º e 7 de outubro de 2026, entre seguidores e não seguidores e por superfície de distribuição.

O relator também seguiu recomendação do Ministério Público Eleitoral e enviou os dados à Presidência do TSE para avaliar se é o caso de determinar uma fiscalização extraordinária no acordo fechado pela plataforma com a Justiça Eleitoral.

Bellize afirmou ainda que a decisão aplica-se às duas campanhas, com efeitos até o fim do pleito.

"As medidas determinadas observam a mínima intervenção da Justiça Eleitoral no debate democrático: não alcançam o conteúdo das manifestações, não asseguram alcance de conteúdo na internet a nenhuma candidatura, aplicam-se igualmente a ambas e cessam com o término do segundo turno", acrescentou.

Em nota, a Meta disse nesta sexta que a empresa "não toma partido nessa nem em nenhuma outra eleição", afirmou que a conta do presidente e candidato à reeleição Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) chegou a ser suspensa "por engano" e que "incidentes técnicos recentes" afetaram as duas campanhas na internet.

De acordo com o posicionamento, uma "lacuna" nas "proteções" da empresa fez com que a ferramenta de inteligência artificial da Meta elaborasse materiais de campanha que favoreciam o senador e também candidato Flávio Bolsonaro (PL).

"Nossos sistemas não classificam nem distribuem conteúdo com base em ideologia política, e nossas regras e sua aplicação valem igualmente para todos", declarou a empresa na nota.

Pela Lei das Eleições, a criação de imagens sobre candidatos por meio de assistentes de inteligência artificial é proibido.

A resolução 23.755/2026 do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) proíbe "emitir opiniões, indicar preferência eleitoral, recomendar voto ou realizar qualquer forma de favorecimento ou desfavorecimento político-eleitoral, de maneira direta ou indireta, inclusive por meio de respostas automatizadas".

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro concede entrevista à Globo | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do PL fala à jornalista Renata Lo Prete, da TV Globo. Presidente Lula (PT), que tenta a reeleição, foi entrevistado nessa quinta-feira (15).
articles.summary: Candidato do PL fala à jornalista Renata Lo Prete, da TV Globo. Presidente Lula (PT), que tenta a reeleição, foi entrevistado nessa quinta-feira (15).
articles.body:
Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) já está na bancada para ser entrevistado por Renata Lo Prete. — Foto: Globo/ Manoella Mello

O candidato à Presidência pelo PL, senador Flávio Bolsonaro , concede nesta sexta-feira (16) entrevista à Globo.

A entrevista, conduzida pela jornalista Renata Lo Prete direto dos Estúdios Globo, no Rio, faz parte da cobertura do segundo turno das Eleições 2026 .

O programa é transmitido pela TV Globo, pela GloboNews e pelo g1.

Confira os principais temas da entrevista de Flávio Bolsonaro à Globo:

O senador Flávio Bolsonaro foi questionado sobre suas propostas para fazer ajuste fiscal e afirmou que vai manter o reajuste de salário mínimo vinculado à inflação, que não vai desvincular o percentual de reajuste para corrigir aposentadorias e que não vai eliminar pisos de gasto com saúde e educação.

"Importante suas perguntas, porque têm circulado, de fato, muitas fake news, e esse é um importante momento para esclarecê-las, porque o meu concorrente está promovendo um verdadeiro terrorismo", disse.

O senador afirmou que, sem mexer nestes três pontos, o reajuste nas contas públicas virá de corte de "ao menos dez ministérios" e que parte dos gastos estão vinculados à corrupção e à má gestão de estatais.

"Se pegar os quase R$ 3 trilhões de dívidas que a União tem a receber, isso pode ser securitizado, trazemos mais de R$ 200 bilhões a mais de receita para esse orçamento por ano, para cada ano é possível alcançar essa cifra", disse Flávio, ao citar os royalties do petróleo como outra fonte de receitas.

Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) afirmou que mudou de posição sobre o fim da escala 6x1 após ouvir trabalhadores durante a campanha e negou que vá reverter a medida caso seja eleito presidente.

Questionado sobre ter chamado a proposta de eleitoreira e oportunista antes de votar a favor dela, o senador declarou que decidiu acompanhar a vontade da maioria dos trabalhadores.

“Eu rodei o Brasil inteiro, ouvi muitos trabalhadores e votei conforme o que vi nas ruas. Como ouvi da grande maioria dos trabalhadores que eles estavam a favor do fim da escala 6 por 1, resolvi seguir a vontade da maioria dos trabalhadores brasileiros”, afirmou.

Ao ser questionado sobre a intenção de aliados de retomar uma proposta do PL que previa salários proporcionais às horas trabalhadas, negou que fosse atuar para reverter o fim da escala.

“Não vou, Renata. Foi uma decisão do Congresso Nacional. Então, da minha parte, nenhum questionamento com relação a isso”, declarou.

O presidente Lula, que tenta a reeleição, abriu a série de entrevistas da Globo com os candidatos que disputam a Presidência neste segundo turno. A ordem das entrevistas foi definida por sorteio em reunião com representantes das campanhas.

Na entrevista a Renata Lo Prete nessa quinta-feira (15), Lula defendeu a redução da maioridade penal no caso de crimes hediondos e pediu a investigação de ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) suspeitos de envolvimento no caso Master. Veja aqui o que o presidente disse à Globo.

A entrevista de Flávio Bolsonaro pode ser acompanhada ao vivo pelos seguintes canais e plataformas:

Globoplay : entrevista completa disponível após a exibição;

g1 : conteúdo na íntegra após a transmissão.

Quando será o debate presidencial da Globo?

Foram convidados Lula (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). O encontro será realizado nos Estúdios Globo, no Rio de Janeiro , e mediado pelo jornalista César Tralli.

O debate será transmitido ao vivo pela TV Globo, com exibição simultânea pela GloboNews e pelo g1, logo após o Jornal Nacional.

articles.title: Chuva causa deslizamento de barranco e afeta tubulação de água em PP | G1
articles.standfirst: Ocorrência foi registrada próximo à Avenida Miguel Damha, em direção à Rodovia Júlio Budisk (SP-501). Equipes técnicas da Sabesp estavam no local.
articles.summary: As fortes chuvas que atingiram a região nesta sexta-feira (16) causaram um deslizamento de barranco próximo à Avenida Miguel Damha, em Presidente Prudente (SP).
articles.body:
Chuvas causam deslizamento de barranco e rompimento de tubulação de água em Prudente (SP) — Foto: Reprodução/Defesa Civil

As fortes chuvas que atingiram a região nesta sexta-feira (16) provocaram um deslizamento de barranco em Presidente Prudente (SP), que rompeu uma tubulação de água nas proximidades da Avenida Miguel Damha, no sentido da Rodovia Júlio Budisk (SP-501).

Conforme a Defesa Civil, houve um deslizamento de barranco na rede de distribuição da Companhia de Saneamento Básico do Estado de São Paulo (Sabesp). As equipes da companhia foram acionadas para atuar no local no período da manhã desta sexta-feira.

A Prefeitura de Presidente Prudente informou que equipes da Defesa Civil e da Secretaria de Obras estiveram no local, onde foi identificada a rachadura na lateral da pista por causa das fortes chuvas que atingiram o município.

Segundo a prefeitura, devido à manutenção da tubulação pela Sabesp, parte da pista foi interditada, deixando o tráfego de veículos apenas por um trecho. A orientação aos motoristas que passam pelo local é para redobrar a atenção.

Em nota, a Sabesp informou que as equipes técnicas permamecem no local realizando os serviços de manutenção para restabelecer o funcionamento da rede. Conforme a companhia, cerca de 20 imóveis foram afetados pela interrupção temporária do abastecimento.

A previsão é de que os trabalhos sejam concluídos durante a noite desta sexta-feira, com a retomada gradativa do abastecimento após a conclusão do reparo. O prazo para a normalização completa poderia variar conforme as condições operacionais do sistema.

A Sabesp informou que permanece à disposição dos clientes pelos canais de atendimento pelo telefone 0800 055 0195 (ligação gratuita), pelo WhatsApp (11) 3388-8000 e pela Agência Virtual .

articles.title: Datafolha: 96% pretendem ir votar no 2º turno; 1% diz que não vai | G1
articles.standfirst: Outros 3% disseram que ainda não se decidiram. Margem de erro é de 2 pontos para mais ou para menos.
articles.summary: Outros 3% disseram que ainda não se decidiram. Margem de erro é de 2 pontos para mais ou para menos.
articles.body:
Pesquisa Datafolha divulgada nesta sexta-feira (16) indica que 96% dos eleitores brasileiros pretendem ir votar no 2º turno, em 25 de outubro. Outro 1% diz que não tem a intenção de comparecer às urnas.

No 1º turno da eleição presidencial, mais de 21% dos eleitores não compareceram aos locais de votação, o que representa mais de 33 milhões de eleitores.

Entre os eleitores que dizem ter a intenção de votar em Lula (PT), 98% responderam que pretendem ir votar e 2% responderam que ainda não se decidiram. Os mesmos indicadores foram registrados entre os eleitores de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL): 98% dizem que vão votar, enquanto 2% ainda estão indecisos.

Os brasileiros que responderam que pretendem votar em branco, nulo ou não votar em nenhum candidato: 63% responderam que têm a intenção de comparecer às urnas, 23% que não devem ir votar e 13% estão indecisos.

O Datafolha foi contratado pelo jornal Folha de S.Paulo e ouviu 2.520 eleitores de terça (13) a quarta-feira (14). A margem de erro é de 2 pontos percentuais para mais ou menos, e o nível de confiança é de 95%. A pesquisa está registrada no TSE (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral) sob o código BR-00466/2026.

Entre os 4% de eleitores que não devem ir votar ou que estão indecisos, o Datafolha aponta que 47% citam a indecisão sobre candidatos como razão para ficarem em casa ou não terem definido o que vão fazer. Neste grupo, a margem de erro é de 10 pontos para mais ou menos .

Outros 27%, que têm dúvidas entre os dois concorrentes, já 20% responderam que não gostam de nenhum candidato. Veja os números:

Entre quem não vai votar ou está indeciso, os motivos são:

Não gosta de eleição/de ir votar/não está com vontade de votar: 11%

Não tem obrigatoriedade de votar pela idade: 4%

O ganhador já está definido/o voto não irá mudar o resultado: 1%

articles.title: Tish James confronted on camera over Trump's accusation of bias in Cornell rape case
articles.summary: Letitia James vows a fair probe into the alleged Cornell University gang rape, but Trump and defense attorneys question her impartiality.
articles.body: New York Attorney General Letitia James on Friday vowed to conduct a "fair" investigation into the seven defendants accused of sexually assaulting an unnamed woman at a fraternity party at Cornell University. James’ investigation into the alleged college gang rape was launched after the filing of a recent lawsuit against Cornell University, the Chi Phi fraternity and several other defendants that has thrust the Ivy League university’s handling of campus sexual assault into the national spotlight. The remarks to a reporter come as James has repeatedly pushed back on questions about her impartiality, insisting the investigation will be guided by the facts and evidence, not politics. President Donald Trump, a longtime foe of the attorney general, has also questioned James' ability to lead an impartial investigation. Trump made the remarks after Fox News' Peter Doocy asked for his view on Hochul appointing James as special prosecutor in the case. LETITIA JAMES FACES NEW PUSH TO BOOT HER FROM CORNELL RAPE PROBE OVER ALLEGED BIAS: COURT DOCUMENTS "Letitia James is a corrupt person," Trump said. "She’s totally corrupt, and I can’t imagine it. And I feel badly for whoever she’s looking at because they won’t get a fair shake. Letitia James is a corrupt person." Attorneys for two of the defendants have also sought James’ removal, including Andrew Miltenberg, who represents Gillio Lopes, and Teny Geragos, who represents Winston Lee. The defense attorneys point to a social media post by James that Geragos separately argued in a court filing shows she is "unquestionably biased." Just days before Hochul's appointment, James posted on X in support of the alleged victim, identified in court filings as Jane Doe. "What this young woman has been forced to endure is horrific and unacceptable. I’m holding her in my heart and in my prayers," James posted on X Sept. 28. "To her, and to all survivors: you’re not alone. We stand with you." Hochul has stood by her appointment of James amid the criticism, saying she has "every confidence" the attorney general will "look at the facts, examine the record and draw the proper conclusions." James has rejected accusations that she prejudged the case, saying during an attorney general campaign debate that her comments supporting the alleged victim were intended to demonstrate "empathy" and insisting that "politics stops at the door" of her office. CORNELL RAPE ALLEGATIONS PROMPT NY ATTORNEY GENERAL LETITIA JAMES TO OPEN ‘ACTIVE CRIMINAL INVESTIGATION’ SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER The case centers on allegations from a Cornell student that she was gang raped at a Chi Phi fraternity house party in 2024. Her allegations were investigated by Cornell University Police, which submitted her six-page sworn statement to the Tompkins County District Attorney’s Office. Prosecutors declined to pursue charges at the time, concluding that the conduct described in the statement did not provide sufficient evidence to sustain criminal charges under New York law. articles.title: Loomer lobbies to replace Zacharia: ‘Hear me out’
articles.summary: Far-right activist Laura Loomer put herself forward as a candidate for White House press secretary as Katie Zacharia was ousted from the role Friday after just five days. In three separate posts on the social platform X, the conservative influencer argued her case. “Here me out: Press Secretary Laura Loomer,” she wrote in an initial…
articles.body:
Far-right activist Laura Loomer put herself forward as a candidate for White House press secretary as Katie Zacharia was ousted from the role Friday after just five days.

In three separate posts on the social platform X , the conservative influencer argued her case .

“Here me out: Press Secretary Laura Loomer,” she wrote in an initial post.

Two hours later, Loomer followed up by stating she would “be an amazing Press Secretary.”

“I’d show President Trump all the receipts,” she continued. “I would bring my binder full of receipts to every briefing.”

Loomer also posted an image of her face poorly cropped onto an image of a woman with long blond hair. Both Zacharia and her predecessor , former press secretary Karoline Leavitt, have blond hair.

The Hill has reached out to the White House for comment on Loomer’s posts.

Zacharia faced criticism after she cut short her first press briefing Tuesday, appearing visibly nervous and only taking three questions from White House reporters. Additionally, questions regarding her legal background have garnered scrutiny this week .

Loomer defended Zacharia in a Friday X post , accusing critics of being “unnecessarily cruel.”

“I wish Katie the best,” Loomer wrote. “I think it’s great that President Trump has people who are so devoted to his cause they are willing to subject themselves to public nitpicking on a daily basis. I’m sure he appreciates it and I think Katie had good intentions.”

Prior to Zacharia’s appointment as press secretary, several Trump allies were floated as possible contenders to replace Leavitt, including White House deputy press secretary Anna Kelly, former acting U.S. Attorney for New Jersey Alina Habba, former Department of Homeland Security Assistant Secretary Tricia McLaughlin and conservative commentator Scott Jennings.

On Friday, prediction market Kalshi had Jennings as the top contender to fill the role, followed by Kelly and conservative author Elizabeth Pipko.

Trump told Fox News’s senior White House correspondent Peter Doocy following the news of Zacharia’s departure on Friday that he was not in a rush to fill the vacancy.

articles.body:
President Trump will campaign in Michigan next week, marking what is slated to be his seventh campaign stop in a seven-day stretch.

The Republican National Committee on Friday said Trump will headline a rally in St. Clair County, Mich., on Oct. 25 following an appearance in Macon, Ga., the day prior.

Trump’s midterm travel schedule is packed next week. On Monday, he will rally Republicans in Wichita, Kan., before heading to Greenville, N.C., on Tuesday. The president will then campaign in Clemson, S.C., on Wednesday, Sioux City, Iowa, on Thursday and Fort Myers, Fla., on Friday.

Michigan is home to highly competitive gubernatorial, Senate and House races. The state’s Senate race has been in the national spotlight, with many Democrats saying they are growing increasingly optimistic about Democrat Abdul El-Sayed’s chances of winning.

Progressive Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.) campaigned with El-Sayed in the Wolverine State this week, and former President Obama is set to campaign there on Oct. 24 — a day before Trump’s visit.

Vice President Vance campaigned with Republican Senate nominee, former Rep. Mike Rogers (R-Mich.), on Thursday.

While Rogers has appeared with Trump on the campaign trail in Michigan, he has made an effort to distance himself from some of the president’s policies — including his tariffs and trade war with Canada.

articles.title: Press secretary under Clinton says Zacharia was ‘set up to fail’
articles.summary: Katie Zacharia was set up to fail by the White House and President Trump, who made her White House press secretary without preparing her, former Clinton-era White House press secretary Joe Lockhart said Friday. “I don’t mean this to sound partisan or overly critical of the president, but she is, in fact a victim here,”…
articles.body:
Katie Zacharia was set up to fail by the White House and President Trump, who made her White House press secretary without preparing her, former Clinton-era White House press secretary Joe Lockhart said Friday.

“I don’t mean this to sound partisan or overly critical of the president, but she is, in fact a victim here,” Lockhart said during an appearance on CNN . “She was thrown out there in a place where she wasn’t prepared.”

Lockhart said when he got the job of press secretary, he took two months off to go to school, sit down with the national security team, budget team and essentially get prepared.

“I wasn’t going to go out, the president wasn’t going to let me go out, the staff wasn’t — until I was absolutely ready, and that’s when I went out,” he said. “She did this in a couple of hours.“

“She was set up to fail , and she has failed. But it shouldn’t be surprising,” he added. “There ought to be a little bit of sympathy here for her that she was not given the ability to succeed here.”

Zacharia, who was appointed to the position a week ago, is “transitioning out” of her role after Trump told reporters that he told her to “reconsider” the position, a White House official told The Hill.

She got off to a rocky start after facing scrutiny about her claims of being a lawyer as reports surfaced about her not being licensed to practice law in any U.S. state. Watchdog group Campaign for Accountability filed a complaint with the State Bar of California asking for an investigation into her claim.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Zacharia failed her California bar exam after she received her law degree from Pepperdine University. She said Thursday that the results of the test are “ somewhat inconsequential. ”

Zacharia ran her first press briefing Tuesday, which lasted 14 minutes, taking three questions from reporters and dropping the news about the resignation of U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle.

Zacharia lasted just five days in the role.

articles.title: Watchdog: Zacharia’s exit doesn’t ‘wipe clean’ dispute over legal credentials
articles.summary: A D.C.-based ethics watchdog group that accused Katie Zacharia of misrepresenting herself as a lawyer is urging the State Bar of California to press ahead with an investigation into her credentials after she was reportedly ousted as White House press secretary. The Campaign for Accountability, which filed a bar complaint against Zacharia earlier this week, said her exit from the…
articles.body:
A D.C.-based ethics watchdog group that accused Katie Zacharia of misrepresenting herself as a lawyer is urging the State Bar of California to press ahead with an investigation into her credentials after she was reportedly ousted as White House press secretary.

The Campaign for Accountability, which filed a bar complaint against Zacharia earlier this week, said her exit from the White House does not resolve allegations that she may have violated California law by portraying herself as a lawyer despite never being licensed to practice law.

“The White House clearly recognized that keeping Katie Zacharia as Press Secretary was untenable given the facts that have come out about her conduct,” Michelle Kuppersmith, the group’s executive director, said in a Friday statement to The Hill.

“Even so, her departure does not wipe clean the fact that she consistently, and apparently falsely, held herself out as a lawyer,” Kuppersmith added. “This is a crime in California, so we continue to urge the state’s Bar to investigate and impose any appropriate penalties.”

The group filed its complaint Wednesday, the day after Zacharia’s brief tenure got off to a rocky start with a shaky first press briefing and scrutiny into her professional history.

Zacharia, a graduate of Pepperdine Caruso School of Law, has often referred to herself in media appearances as a “lawyer” despite never having passed the bar exam. Her LinkedIn profile also referenced her role as “general counsel” for Fix California, a conservative nonprofit founded by President Trump ally and former administration official Richard Grenell.

She has claimed to have worked as an associate on the International Practice Team of Beijing-based Zhong Lun Law Firm, and Trump described her as an “attorney” when he announced her as former press secretary Karoline Leavitt’s replacement.

When asked by reporters on the South Lawn this week which state she took the bar exam in, Zacharia replied, “When I moved to China.” She later said she misheard the question due to the noise of Marine One and assumed it was about where she went after law school.

In subsequent interviews, she admitted she never passed the California bar exam, telling The New York Times the results were “somewhat inconsequential” since she was planning to move overseas at the time.

“It was never my intent to go into the practice of law,” Zacharia told Fox News’s Sean Hannity Thursday night. “When I went to go engage in media and give legal analysis, I consulted attorneys and legal professionals as to whether or not they agreed that I could be labeled a lawyer, both because I had a valid Juris Doctor from a good law school, a reputable law school, Pepperdine Law School, and in conjunction with the fact that I did have actual substantive legal experience.”

The watchdog group alleges her use of the terms may have been unlawful because each representation “conveys to an ordinary listener that Ms. Zacharia is a licensed attorney entitled to practice law.”

It is commonly believed the term “lawyer” refers to someone who has graduated from law school, while an “attorney” is someone who has passed the bar exam and is licensed to practice law in a specific jurisdiction.

But the American Bar Association makes no such distinction, using the titles interchangeably to describe any “licensed professional who advises and represents others in legal matters.” Many state licensing statutes, including California’s, don’t either.

California law asserts that “no person shall practice law” in the state unless that person is “an active member of the State Bar” and makes it a misdemeanor offense to unlawfully portray oneself as “practicing or entitled to practice law.”

It remains to be seen what outcome could come from the complaint, if the State Bar of California even chooses to pursue it at all. Data compiled by Vitreo , an independent hub for judicial data, shows that disciplinary agencies process tens of thousands of complaints each year, and the vast majority are dismissed, screened out or resolved privately.

Because Zacharia is not a member of the California Bar, the agency can’t take any professional disciplinary action against her even if it identifies wrongdoing. It could, however, refer her for prosecution on criminal charges.

The White House confirmed Friday afternoon that Zacharia was “transitioning out” of the role just five days after Trump announced her as his pick to fill the press secretary role.

articles.summary: Presented by Coalition to Strengthen Americas Healthcare {beacon} Healthcare Healthcare The Big Story Senate Democrats unveil new plans for strengthening Medicare Led by Sen. Ron Wyden (R-Ore.), ranking member of the Senate Finance Committee, Senate Democrats on Friday published their aims of revamping the long-term care system in the U.S., encompassing both home care and…
articles.body:
Senate Democrats unveil new plans for strengthening Medicare

Led by Sen. Ron Wyden (R-Ore.), ranking member of the Senate Finance Committee, Senate Democrats on Friday published their aims of revamping the long-term care system in the U.S., encompassing both home care and nursing homes.

In a request for information (RFI), Wyden stated, “It has been decades since Congress enacted a comprehensive, system-level investment in long-term care infrastructure and financing. And a system-level investment is what is needed.”

The document serves as something of a blueprint for what Democrats hope to achieve in the Medicare space if they reclaim Congress in the upcoming midterms.

At the top of their list is the goal of making long-term care universally available to all Americans.

“Throughout 95 listening sessions, Senate Democrats heard repeatedly about the importance of establishing universal coverage for LTC. articles.body:
GOP senators press Pentagon over Starlink restrictions in Ukraine

Four Republican senators joined their Democratic colleagues in pressing the Trump administration for information about whether Pentagon officials ordered restrictions on Ukraine’s access to the satellite-based Starshield network .

Ukraine needs access to fast Starshield data speeds to operate drones, along with fixed-wing and rotary-wing aircraft — which are critical to its national defense.

Ukraine’s full access to Starshield-provided data was quickly restored Wednesday, prompting speculation on Capitol Hill that President Trump didn’t make the call to cut off intelligence sharing with Ukraine but that the decision may have come from senior officials.

Four Republican senators — including two senior members of the Senate Intelligence Committee — signed a bipartisan letter to Platte Moring, the Pentagon’s inspector general, demanding he investigate whether any Defense Department or other U.S. government officials “directed” or “authorized” changes to intelligence-sharing arrangements or Starlink and Starshield services affecting Ukraine.

Starshield is the military version of SpaceX’s Starlink, which provides internet connectivity from low-orbit satellites.

Senate Appropriations Committee Chair Susan Collins (R-Maine), a senior member of the Intelligence Committee, signed the letter, along with fellow panel member Sen. John Cornyn (R-Texas), as well as Republican Sens. Lisa Murkowski (Alaska) and Thom Tillis (N.C.).

The GOP lawmakers expressed “grave concern ” over reports that Ukraine lost access to high-speed internet connectivity, which enables it to operate military vehicles flying faster than 63 mph or faster than 100 mph. The loss hampered its ability to fend off Russian strikes.

A Senate source familiar with internal discussions about how to respond to Ukraine’s sudden loss of access to critical military intelligence said senators in both parties have questions about whether Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth or other senior Pentagon officials — such as Elbridge Colby, the undersecretary of defense for policy — were involved in the decision.

articles.summary: U.S. energy regulators have proposed establishing a program that would speed up approvals for expanding the nation’s gas export facilities The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) proposed Thursday to limit notice and protest periods to either 60 or 90 days for requested expansions to liquified natural gas (LNG) export terminals. articles.body:
U.S. energy regulators have proposed establishing a program that would speed up approvals for expanding the nation’s gas export facilities

The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) proposed Thursday to limit notice and protest periods to either 60 or 90 days for requested expansions to liquified natural gas (LNG) export terminals.

FERC Chair Laura Swett (R) said the move would “enable the country to scale up its existing facilities more quickly to supply our allies who are in desperate need.”

She added that the action would “maintain safety and environmental protections.”

The commission also proposed to no longer require planned gas projects to submit certain air pollution information as part of the environmental review process.

Specifically, the commission is looking to omit air dispersion models, which simulate how a project’s emissions may interact with other atmospheric pollution to determine air quality impacts.

“These models have proven time and again to be an unnecessary source of confusion, delay, and litigation risk,” Swett said.

However, fellow FERC commissioner Judy Chang (D) disagreed, saying this type of modeling is “the best tool we have for understanding the likely local and regional air impacts of the projects we permit.”

Both moves by the commission received pushback from environmental advocates.

“It is unconscionable for FERC to further fast-track harmful LNG development and also cut requirements for gas developers to submit modeling to understand the local air quality impacts of methane gas projects,” Claire Dorner, Sierra Club’s associate legislative and advocacy director of its “Beyond Dirty Fuels” campaign, said in a written statement.

“Eroding these guardrails will make our historically high energy prices even worse, increase harm to local ecosystems and communities, and exacerbate the climate crisis,” Dorner said.

FERC is made up of presidentially appointed commissioners but is technically independent from the Trump administration. It is comprised of three Republicans and two Democrats.

articles.title: 5 days of Katie Zacharia: The rapid fall of Trump’s ‘lawyer’ press secretary
articles.summary: Katie Zacharia won’t be remembered as one of the “all-time greats” in the White House press room, as one of her colleagues predicted this week, but she will go down in the annals of presidential press secretary history. Her tenure of five days in the role easily beats the previous record held by Anthony Scaramucci,…
articles.body:
Katie Zacharia won’t be remembered as one of the “all-time greats” in the White House press room, as one of her colleagues predicted this week, but she will go down in the annals of presidential press secretary history.

Her tenure of five days in the role easily beats the previous record held by Anthony Scaramucci, who spent 11 days in President Trump’s communications shop during his first term.

Zacharia kicked off her time at the podium with some big news, announcing the departure of Kimberly Guilfoyle as U.S. ambassador to Greece, but she quickly became the news as questions swirled over her legal career.

Trump announced Monday, a federal holiday, that Zacharia would be holding her first press briefing the next day.

“Katie has been with me, in spirit, from the very beginning, and will do a fantastic job!” he wrote on Truth Social.

Before the appointment, she was the senior communications adviser to Truth Social, after having briefly served as a spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security.

Zacharia was seen on the South Lawn as Trump departed for a campaign rally in Ohio Monday afternoon but stayed behind at the White House. She received her initial briefing materials that same day.

Zacharia held her first press briefing before a packed room of journalists. It was a shaky opening as she haltingly read from a script and accidentally referred to her husband, Tyler Zacharia, as “my president.”

She broke the major news about Guilfoyle, which led the ensuing news cycle, but only spoke for roughly 14 minutes and took questions from three conservative-leaning outlets.

Within minutes, critics were asking if Zacharia was up for the job, but her defenders said the nerves were to be expected during her first outing in the pressure-packed press room.

That afternoon, a reporter asked Trump where his new press secretary, who often touted herself as a lawyer, passed the bar exam. He turned around to Zacharia, standing behind him outside the White House, to answer.

She responded , “When I moved to China.”

The newsletter Popular Information previously raised questions about her legal career, reporting that no record was found of her passing a bar exam anywhere.

The White House said Zacharia moved to China with her husband after graduating from Pepperdine University’s law school.

She had referred to herself as a lawyer on TV previously, and Trump called her an attorney when he announced she would be taking the position.

Her LinkedIn account shows she worked as an associate at the Zhong Lun Law Firm in Beijing from August 2011 to June 2013 and was general counsel of Fix California from 2024 to 2025.

Both resume items would become the subject of much chatter in the days ahead.

The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday that she sat for the California bar exam after graduating from law school in 2011 but didn’t pass.

The Campaign for Accountability filed a complaint with the State Bar of California on Wednesday asking for an investigation into whether Zacharia’s claims of being a lawyer broke state law.

The complaint notes that if the reporting is accurate — that Zacharia has “repeatedly held herself out to the public as entitled to practice law without a license to do so” — it could be a crime under California law.

The White House pushed back on the complaint, with communications director Steven Cheung calling Campaign for Accountability a “radical leftist-organization run by rabid numbskulls suffering from a severe case of Trump Derangement Syndrome.”

Zacharia’s time in China also came under the spotlight. Legal experts told The Hill that while she may have worked at a law firm in China, that didn’t necessarily make her a lawyer.

Zacharia went on defense Thursday, with a pair of interviews on conservative outlets.

She told Jack Posobiec on Real America’s Voice that she didn’t have time to get fully prepared ahead of the shaky Tuesday briefing.

“I never had a full briefing beforehand, and I went out and I effectuated the briefing,” she said.

“It was absolutely my goal to keep it short, considering he is his own best spokesperson,” she added of Trump.

She said the initial briefing materials were given to her Monday evening but were only finalized Tuesday at 8 a.m., less than two hours before she appeared for the 9:30 a.m. briefing. She said she had been up since 3 a.m. preparing.

She told Posobiec that the results of her bar exam were “somewhat inconsequential” because she knew she’d be moving to China.

“After moving to China, I didn’t really think much of the bar results or consider that something that I needed to focus on,” she said.

“It’s unfortunate that people dub this as some kind of conspiracy or want to put me in a camp,” she said. “The truth is, I was very careful how I executed this, and I never came across as someone who was an attorney-at-law.”

Zacharia faced a surprisingly hostile Sean Hannity on Fox News Thursday evening.

“You called it a conspiracy theory as it relates to being a lawyer,” Hannity said, referencing the interview Zacharia did with Posobiec, pointing out what he said were 15 social media posts “where you identify yourself as an attorney.”

“I think they were retweets, and I corrected the record,” she responded.

Zacharia appeared on Fox News again Friday morning and was again met with tough questions.

“Fox & Friends” host Lawrence Jones asked if she should have told the White House about her legal qualifications during the hiring process.

“Those questions weren’t asked,” she said. “I’m being hired as White House press secretary, not White House counsel. The conversations and the reason I was — the reason that I was hired was to represent the president in the press.”

She said the “legacy media wants to put the focus and attention on me because they wanted to be distracted from the major wins that President Trump is making for America.”

If the interviews were meant to win over Trump, it didn’t work.

Later Friday, Trump told reporters before departing the White House that he told Zacharia to “reconsider” the role .

“I said, ‘Honestly, if I were you, I’d reconsider,’” Trump told reporters Friday, referring to a conversation he said he had with Zacharia earlier.

“I said, ‘You think about it, but I would reconsider,’” he continued.

Minutes later came the first reports that she was out of the job.

A White House official said she was “transitioning out” of the role.

Zacharia hasn’t made any public comments and did not respond to a request for comment from The Hill.

A source familiar told The Hill that Zacharia was to join Vice President Vance and second lady Usha Vance for dinner at their residence Friday evening.

articles.title: Oregon teacher fought school attacker before armed dad killed suspect
articles.summary: The 16-year-old suspect previously attended the primary school and had targeted a special educational needs classroom, police say.
articles.body:
An Oregon teacher threw her mobile phone before she tackled and tried to wrestle away a shotgun from the arms of a teen suspect who opened fire on a special educational needs class.

As she tussled with him on the floor of the class - where three children and a teacher were killed - a bystander ran inside. Armed with a .40-caliber pistol, he opened fire and killed the teen.

The bystander, a dad of two girls at the school, had been driving past Silver Rail Elementary in Bend when he saw the suspect firing in the car park then shooting through a window to enter.

The details of the Thursday attack were confirmed by police, who said the 16-year-old suspect was a prior student at the school.

Police say the suspect was armed with about 44 more rounds of shotgun ammunition when he was stopped. He fired as many as 15 rounds in the class.

"To the people who showed courage in the face of such violence, and intervened to prevent this tragedy from being any worse, we owe you a debt of gratitude," Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said on Friday.

Police offered more information on the attack at at a news conference on Friday, where they identified two of the four victims. They include five-year-old Rhoam Summer and 25-year-old teacher Meghan Lambert.

The families of the two other students who were killed, an eight-year-old and 11-year-old, did not wish to have them publicly identified yet, police said.

Two others were injured in the attack. Another teacher, a 54-year-old, was still being treated at hospital, and a seven-year-old student, who was in serious but stable condition.

Krantz said the heroic actions of both the teacher and the father who ran inside the school saved lives.

He said the teacher who wrestled with the gunman was not hurt but "almost certainly helped prevent more bloodshed".

He identified the suspect as 16-year-old Griffin J. John II, who previously attended the school and was a special educational needs student there.

A search warrant has been executed at the suspect's home and a search is ongoing, the police chief said.

Police believe the suspect travelled to the elementary school on foot, but police are still investigating his exact movements and how he acquired the gun. A motive is also not clear.

Officials did not confirm the name of the father who intervened and fatally shot the suspect.

But Kaylub Giamanco's family has identified him to US media as the person who sprang into action.

The 36-year-old carpenter had just finished lunch and was on his way home when he passed the school, his brother told NBC News. He saw the suspect open fire on a vehicle outside the school then shoot through a window and go inside.

Police said he had a legally concealed .40 caliber in his vehicle and his brother said he grabbed the pistol "and decided to go in after" the suspect. Police say he fired at the suspect "multiple times", killing him.

In a statement to the BBC's partner CBS News, Giamanco's family said he is a "lifelong resident of Bend" and that he "is not seeking recognition".

The family said Giamanco wants to express his "gratitude to the first responders, school personnel, and community for the outpouring of love and support". He and his family "respectfully ask for privacy".

US President Donald Trump praised the bystander's actions on Friday, calling him a "great hero".

Addressing reporters at the White House before departing for Georgia, Trump said the situation could have been "much worse" with no intervention.

"It's a terrible thing, but thank goodness for a man that had a gun and knew how to use it," he said.

Without naming the bystander, Governor Kotek acknowledged the man's heroic actions stopping further loss of life, but noted they "carry a heavy emotional burden, and I just want you to know that my thoughts are with you as well".

Kayla Epstein contributed to this report.

articles.summary: Katy Padilla Stout's Texas Democratic campaign reported over $4,300 in cookies, beer and wine and Mexican restaurant spending, according to FEC records.
articles.body: A Texas Democratic congressional candidate's campaign reported more than $4,300 in spending on cookies, Mexican restaurant purchases and beer and wine earlier this year, according to federal election records, drawing renewed attention after a heated debate in which she apologized for a remark about her Republican opponent "making fun of Nazis." Katy Padilla Stout, the Democrat nominee for Texas' 23rd Congressional District, reported expenditures totaling $4,338.14 in five transactions in March and April, according to spending details cited in an August report by RedState and records attributed to the Federal Election Commission (FEC). The reported purchases included $675 for cookies for a campaign event, $1,289.22 at Total Wine and $2,373.92 at Las Guitarras Cocina Mexicana. SENATE REPUBLICAN SETTLES SIX-YEAR-OLD CAMPAIGN BILL AFTER BEING CALLED OUT ON SOCIAL MEDIA The expenditures have also become a line of attack for Republican Brandon Herrera, whose campaign website showcases the cookie purchase and accuses Stout of using donor funds to pay for the treats. According to the spending details, the campaign reported a $675 payment dated March 30 with the stated purpose "COOKIES FOR EVENT." Herrera's website identifies the payee as Denise Gamboa Zelle and categorizes the expense as a campaign event expenditure. Additional transactions included $1,089.08 at Total Wine on April 21 and $200.14 the following day, both described as "BEER AND WINE." The campaign also reported payments of $2,027.52 and $346.40 to Las Guitarras Cocina Mexicana on April 27 and April 28, respectively, according to the transaction details. In a statement to Fox News Digital, Stout said the disbursements "were for campaign and fundraising events which were attended by our supporters." "Sugar cookies, particularly Texas-shaped ones, hold a special place in Texan culture," she said. "We bought ours at a local bakery because we believe in supporting small businesses." SENATE HOPEFUL'S 'TREADING WATER' NARRATIVE CRUMBLES UNDER $500K CAMPAIGN PAYOUTS TO FAMILY The filings establish that the campaign reported the expenditures but do not establish whether the purchases were improper, whether any were for personal use or how many people attended the associated events. The spending has attracted criticism from Herrera's campaign, which maintains an opposition website, The Real Katy Stout. Under a section labeled "Cookie gate," the site highlights the $675 expenditure and displays the reported purpose, "COOKIES FOR EVENT." The website also criticizes Stout's positions on immigration, taxes and other issues. DEM SENATE NOMINEE APOLOGIZES TO JEWISH VOTERS AFTER 'GENOCIDE' REMARK SPARKED BACKLASH The spending questions come as the two candidates compete for a congressional seat representing one of the country's largest districts along the southern border. During Tuesday's televised debate in San Antonio, Stout also drew attention for an unusual exchange involving Herrera's online videos. "He made millions of dollars after making jokes online, making fun of Nazis, making fun of all of these things that we know he does not need to be doing," Stout said in a heated moment during the debate. Herrera responded, "And here I thought making fun of Nazis was a good thing." Stout later apologized and clarified her criticism after closing remarks. "I apologize, I did misspeak," she said. "He chooses to goose-step on YouTube for clickbait and money so that he can promote that type of ideology. He chooses to shame women." The exchange was part of a debate hosted by WOAI/KABB, during which the congressional candidates also sparred over gun rights, immigration and the cost of living. Stout told Fox News Digital "mocking Nazis is fine, and that is not what I objected to, nor is that what my opponent does." "I object to content that trivializes veteran suicide, rape, child murder, women’s bodies and the Holocaust, the type of content he churns out," she added. "You can hear his disgusting commentary straight from his own mouth at HeReallySaidThat.com. "Do I think he promotes Nazi imagery? Yes. In a video posted 5/24/22, he goose-steps to 'Erika,' and touts an MP-40 machine gun. In another video posted 6/23/20, he said 'for the fatherland' before firing a Nazi-made STG 44, calling it 'like a religious experience.' "Calling it a joke doesn’t change what it is: giving a platform to Nazi symbols and weaponry for clicks and money. In my view, the 'I’m only joking' defense is a familiar tactic among neo-Nazi and antisemitic content creators. His content has attracted bipartisan condemnation, including the Republican Jewish Coalition, which called my opponent 'a goose-stepping extremist who pals around with online Nazis.'" Stout, a former teacher and child welfare attorney, has emphasized affordability and corruption as central themes of her campaign. Herrera, a firearms manufacturer and online personality who has adopted "Let's Go Brandon" as his campaign slogan, has campaigned on border law enforcement, tax reductions and Second Amendment protections. The two are vying to replace former Republican Rep. Tony Gonzales, who resigned earlier this year after acknowledging an affair with a staffer. Texas' 23rd Congressional District stretches from the San Antonio area toward El Paso and includes hundreds of miles of the U.S.-Mexico border.
